sentences.text: Heard both the sides and perused the material on record.

3. This petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., seeking anticipatory bail is preferred by accused No.1 in Crime No.117/2023 of Hassan Women Police Station registered for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 323, 324, 504, 342, 506, 313 r/w 34 of IPC and Section 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
4. Complaint is lodged by the wife of petitioner alleging that her marriage was solemnized with the petitioner on 24.04.2023 as per Hindu customs at one Shubhodaya Kalyana Mantapa, Hassan.
At the time of marriage 180 grams of gold ornaments and Rs.3 lakhs in cash was given as dowry.

She was looked after properly NC: 2024:KHC:10211 only for two months and thereafter, her husband and mother-in-law started demanding further dowry of Rs.5 lakhs and in this connection they were subjecting her to physical and mental torture.
It is further alleged that when she was 1 months pregnant, the accused forced her to abort the child and asked her to do all the household works.
It is also alleged that her husband kicked on her stomach due to which she suffered miscarriage.

5. The learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that there are specific allegations in the complaint that the petitioner has subjected the victim to physical and mental torture and assaulted her with a belt as well as kicked on her stomach due to which, she was admitted at hospital on 18.11.2023 and suffered miscarriage.
He has contended that the offence committed by the petitioner is grave in nature and therefore, he is not entitled for anticipatory bail.
The learned counsel for petitioner has drawn the attention of the Court to the earlier complaint filed by the complainant produced at Annexure-D.
In the said complaint, it is alleged that the couple were in love with each other for about 5 years and about 6 months prior, their marriage was performed by the elders.
Subsequent to the marriage there used to be petty quarrels etc.

It is alleged that the petitioner was in the habit of talking to some woman over phone and send messages and when the complainant questioned about the same, the accused quarreled with her and sent her to her parental home.

It is further alleged that she was abused and driven out of the house etc.
7.
On the basis of the above complaint filed by the wife of the petitioner on 27.10.2023, NCR No.516/2023 was registered by the police.

The complainant's statement dated 28.10.2023 was Venkatesh Gowda T.R vs State Of Karnataka on 13 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94535465/

sentences.text: It goes to show that the elders and family members of the couple intervened and tried to settle the matter.

The complainant has stated that NC: 2024:KHC:10211 if the relationship continues to be uncordial, she will settle the matter before the family Court and further that until her husband provides a separate house, she will stay in her parental home.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that as per the above complaint and statement,
the complainant wanted to live separately with her husband and she has clearly stated that till then she will stay in her parental home.
He therefore contended that it is not specifically stated in her present complaint as to when she returned from her parental home.
He has therefore contended that the entire allegations that the petitioner has assaulted her with a belt and kicked on her stomach and caused abortion etc., is false and baseless.

He would further contend that even though it is alleged by the complainant that on account of the assault by the petitioner she was admitted in the hospital and suffered miscarriage, no MLC was sent by the hospital authority to the police on 18.11.2023.
On the other hand, a written NC: 2024:KHC:10211 complaint was lodged belatedly on 30.11.2023 making false allegations.
9. It appears that there is a serious marital disharmony among the couple, which needs to be resolved by counselling etc.
There is no material placed at this stage except the bald allegation, to show that the complainant suffered miscarriage due to the assault by the petitioner.
The allegations have to be established in due course.
No serious allegations are made in the earlier complaint.
Custodial interrogatin of the petitioner is not required.
Considering the entire facts and circumstances, the relief sought by the petitioner can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER 1. Petition is allowed.
2. Petitioner/accused No.1 in Crime No.117/2023 of Hassan Women Police Station shall be released in NC: 2024:KHC:10211 the event of his arrest, subject to following conditions:
a) He shall appear before the Investigating Officer within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with a surety for the likesum.
b) He shall cooperate with the investigation.
c) He shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is change in the address.
d) He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) He shall not try to intimidate the  complainant.
